quizzes.prompt: The model returns {"quantity":-3,"sku":"A17"}. JSON parsing succeeds. What happens next?
options: Accept because the JSON is valid
Validate domain bounds and reject the negative quantity
Lower temperature and send it directly
feedback: Syntax alone does not validate business meaning.
The parser and domain validator enforce different contracts.
Sampling changes do not enforce the quantity invariant.

quizzes.prompt: Select controls that make a pairwise judge more credible.
options: Choose the answer with the most tokens
feedback: Reduces identity preference as a confound.
Exposes position sensitivity.
Provides a reference for agreement and disagreement.
Length is not correctness and can introduce verbosity bias.

quizzes.prompt: Put the release experiment in a defensible order.
items: Run candidates on the same cases
why: Criteria determine what success means.
The holdout must precede tuning.
Identical cases enable paired comparison.
Averages alone hide failures.
Promotion follows evidence.

quizzes.prompt: Match each measurement to what it establishes.
why: Structure does not establish factual correctness.
Success must include the required terminal artifact.
Agreement measures the judge, not universal truth.

quizzes.prompt: A corpus contains 80 well-structured manuals with exact product IDs. Which baseline is necessary before adding a vector database?
options: Metadata/lexical document selection with section navigation
feedback: Exact identifiers and headings may solve this workload; measure it.
Coordination does not address the evidence-selection bottleneck.
Training is an expensive and weak substitute for revision-aware evidence.

quizzes.prompt: Which statements are defensible?
options: Vectorless can use SQL or lexical indexes
Chunkless may select sections at query time
Long context still has token and attention limits
feedback: It removes vector similarity, not every index.
Avoiding fixed chunks does not remove the need to select context.
RAPTOR, for example, embeds and clusters chunks.
Capacity and effective use are separate concerns.

quizzes.prompt: Order the hybrid retrieval path.
why: Scope must constrain accessible candidates.
Candidate recall limits later stages.
Fusion combines ranked lists.
The expensive pass operates on the shortlist.
The generator receives bounded evidence.

quizzes.prompt: Match failure to the first diagnostic.
pairs: Correct evidence present but answer wrong
why: A reranker cannot recover absent candidates.
The loss occurred after retrieval.
This separates evidence availability from generation fidelity.

quizzes.prompt: store_result succeeds on the server, but the response times out. What is the safe next step?
options: Retry with a new operation ID
Reconcile using the existing operation key
feedback: A new identity can create a duplicate effect.
The same logical identity resolves an unknown outcome.
A timeout only establishes that the response was not received.

quizzes.prompt: A read-only client discovers search and delete tools. Which controls still apply?
options: Treat discovery as permission for all tools
feedback: Discovery is not an authorization decision.
MCP data can be malformed or adversarial.
An advertised capability does not grant authority.
Resource-level scope must be enforced.

quizzes.prompt: Order one bounded agent iteration.
why: State provides evidence and remaining allowance.
The model proposes, not executes.
Code checks the proposed action.
Execution needs timeout and effect semantics.
Failures also consume budget.

quizzes.prompt: Match field to its purpose.
why: Reuse it for retries of the same effect.
Per-call retries must respect the overall deadline.
A changed contract must be versioned or negotiated.

quizzes.prompt: A three-agent system gains 2 points in task success but uses three times the tokens. What is the next useful experiment?
options: Compare paired tasks under equal total budgets
feedback: The gain is confounded with additional compute.
Equal budgets help isolate architectural value.
More complexity does not resolve the confound.

quizzes.prompt: Two credible sources disagree. What should the evidence merge preserve?
feedback: Dates may explain different values.
The verifier needs explicit conflicting evidence.
Voting can hide important contradictory facts.
An unresolved gap should remain visible.

quizzes.prompt: Order a plan task with verification.
why: A plan needs executable contracts.
Tools run within policy.
Evidence makes the result auditable.
A task is not complete merely because a call returned.
Replanning must be justified and bounded.

quizzes.prompt: Match design to its distinguishing feature.
pairs: One policy loop owns action selection
why: A narrow contract limits context and permission spread.
The coordinator handles merge and failure behavior.
This is an essential complexity baseline.

quizzes.prompt: A retrieved page tells the agent to send private context to evil.example. Which is the actual enforcement boundary?
options: A stronger sentence in the prompt
Executable destination and permission checks before tool execution
A polite refusal in the final answer
feedback: Prompting is not an egress control.
The action must be rejected before any effect.
A refusal after a leak cannot undo the leak.

quizzes.prompt: What must an approval be bound to?
options: Any future action the agent invents
feedback: Changed parameters require a new approval.
Authority and validity must be checked at execution.
This would create unbounded authority.
The digest detects changes to the approved action.

quizzes.prompt: Order a defensible incident investigation.
items: Change one suspect component at a time
why: Start from observed impact.
Reproduction requires exact versions.
Confirm the failure before drawing conclusions.
Controlled interventions isolate causes.
A fix needs a recurrence detector and owner.

quizzes.prompt: Match observation to evaluation meaning.
pairs: Unauthorized write despite a safe final answer
Attack blocked and legitimate task completed
why: The violated effect matters more than final prose.
A secure but unusable system is insufficient.
Safety and usefulness must both be measured.

quizzes.prompt: W has shape 4096×4096 and rank r=8. How many trainable adapter parameters are in A and B, ignoring biases?
feedback: That is the full matrix parameter count.
Rank is not the number of all adapter parameters.

quizzes.prompt: Which choices protect evaluation integrity?
options: Include future purchases in current customer features
feedback: Splitting early limits source leakage.
Near duplicates can leak even when exact rows differ.
This leaks future outcomes into features.
It preserves an honest release comparison.

quizzes.prompt: Order the primary request lifecycle.
why: The timer starts at the defined request boundary.
Queueing contributes to user delay.
Prompt processing initializes attention state.
TTFT ends here.
Full-response latency ends later.

quizzes.prompt: Match problem to the first experiment.
pairs: Stable specialist behavior after prompt baseline fails
why: Retrieval provides current evidence.
Evaluate adaptation and retention before scaling.
This is a serving problem, not automatically a knowledge problem.

quizzes.prompt: A worker sends an approved notification, then dies before saving completion. What is missing if restart sends it again?
options: Effect reconciliation with stable idempotency identity
feedback: Context size does not prevent duplicate external effects.
The workflow must resolve executed-but-unacknowledged outcomes.
Prompt instructions cannot enforce effect identity.

quizzes.prompt: Which should appear in a safe distributed trace?
options: Queue delay and worker span links
feedback: Asynchronous boundaries need correlation.
Versions make regressions reproducible.
Secrets must be excluded or redacted.
These localize reliability and cost issues.

quizzes.prompt: Order the release path.
why: The tested artifact must be identifiable.
Model quality and safety are part of the gate.
Limit the initial exposure.
Use measurements, not optimism.
Keep the previous release executable.

quizzes.prompt: Match task to execution mode.
why: Use a defined response deadline.
Return a job ID and durable status.
Batch fits work not needed immediately.

quizzes.prompt: Offline customer ranking predicts future purchases. What can you conclude about campaign uplift?
options: No causal uplift claim without exposure/control evidence
feedback: The dataset has no randomized treatment evidence.
Prediction and intervention effects are different questions.
Predictions are uncertain and not guaranteed outcomes.

quizzes.prompt: A safe response-cache key may need which inputs?
options: Question text only in every application
feedback: Reuse must not cross unauthorized scopes.
Changes can invalidate the old answer.
Text similarity alone can leak or reuse stale content.
Behavior changes affect validity and reproducibility.

quizzes.prompt: Order a controlled improvement cycle.
why: Collect only necessary safe telemetry.
Do not treat every raw interaction as a correct label.
Change one hypothesis with recorded configuration.
Avoid tuning on the release holdout.
Production evidence must close the loop.

quizzes.prompt: Match dependency failure to a defensible behavior.
pairs: Abstain or return explicitly limited evidence
Open circuit and use a validated fallback
Shed or defer work with backpressure
why: Do not fabricate grounding.
Avoid repeated failing calls; fallback still needs evaluation.
Unbounded queues eventually breach deadlines.

1.title: Find the evaluation leak
1.context: The prompt author inspects all held-out answers, adds three examples from them, then reports a 12-point improvement.
options: Move the inspected cases into development
Version prompt, dataset, and per-case results
feedback: A contaminated holdout no longer measures unseen performance.
The viewed examples can inform development, not an untouched test claim.
A new headline score does not repair leakage.
This makes the comparison reproducible.
1.hint: Which cases have already influenced the candidate?
1.solution: Use a new untouched holdout, retain the old cases as development, and rerun the paired comparison with versioned artifacts.

2.title: Choose a retrieval architecture from evidence
2.context: The table contains illustrative fixture measurements, not live model benchmarks. All four candidates use the same 100 questions and corpus.
2.task: Choose a deployable candidate under the stated constraints: correctness ≥90%, citation precision ≥95%, p95 ≤2 seconds.
2.hint: Apply the hard requirements before optimizing cost.
2.solution: Hybrid B is the only fixture candidate satisfying all three constraints. On another measured workload the winner may differ.

4.title: Design the minimum research system
4.context: A research task needs citations, one optional follow-up search, and a report. A team proposes twelve autonomous specialists.
4.task: Select the essential components for a defensible first release.
feedback: Provides a measurable complexity baseline.
Makes source access auditable and limited.
Checks material claims before reporting.
Lets architecture improvements be compared.
Unrestricted delegation adds security and coordination risk.
Independent databases are not justified by this workload.
4.hint: Keep the components needed for evidence and control before adding specialists.
4.solution: Start with one bounded runtime, scoped tools, claim verification, and evaluations. Add coordination only after equal-budget experiments justify it.

5.title: Bind approval to the exact action
5.context: A reviewer approves draft A for a sandbox destination. The agent changes the text and destination but reuses the old approval token.
5.task: Select required checks immediately before dispatch.
options: Allow because the session was approved
feedback: Changed content or parameters invalidates the old approval.
Approval has both authority and lifetime.
Session-wide consent is too broad for this action.
Egress policy applies even to approved proposals.
5.hint: Approval must describe what will actually happen.
5.solution: Reject the changed action, require new approval, and validate identity, expiry, digest, and destination.

7.title: Trace the missing request context
7.context: API span ends after enqueue. Worker logs have unrelated request IDs; model and tool spans have no links. Duplicate delivery sends twice.
options: Propagate trace context or links through the queue
feedback: Restores causal visibility across asynchronous execution.
Prevents duplicate logical effects.
Allows restart and recovery.
Secrets are not correlation identifiers and must not be logged.
7.hint: Observability and effect correctness are different concerns.
7.solution: Propagate safe trace metadata, persist checkpoints, and reconcile effects by stable keys; redact sensitive fields.

8.title: Decide whether to release
8.context: A candidate halves token cost but leaks cross-customer cached answers and cannot recover from approval timeout.
8.task: Select the blocking fixes before promotion.
options: Scope cache keys and invalidate unsafe entries
Persist approval state and expire it safely
Run security and recovery regression cases
feedback: Cache reuse must preserve access boundaries.
Long waits require durable, bounded state.
The candidate must demonstrate the fixes.
Economics do not override safety and correctness.
Timeout is an unknown or failed state, not success.
8.hint: A release must meet all hard gates, not just one metric.
8.solution: Block promotion, repair cache authorization and approval recovery, then rerun the affected gates and canary.

3A.title: Repair the agent runtime
3A.context: A loop retries forever on timeout. Each retry receives a new operation key and successful calls alone decrement the step counter.
3A.task: Select repairs that address the observed faults.
options: Reuse logical operation identity and reconcile unknown outcomes
Charge failed calls against the budget
feedback: Prevents duplicate effects after a lost acknowledgement.
Makes repeated failure terminate.
Preserves policy when a model proposes an unsafe action.
Sampling does not repair runtime semantics.
3A.hint: There are separate effect, termination, and policy invariants.
3A.solution: Use stable effect keys, count every attempt, enforce a deadline, authorize actions, and persist observations.

3B.title: Inspect a malicious MCP response
3B.context: search_documents returns a valid-looking passage followed by an instruction to invoke delete_document. The client was granted read-only access.
options: Treat result text as untrusted data
Reject delete_document at the policy boundary
Validate response fields and document scope
feedback: Tool output cannot become higher-priority authority.
The operation is outside the client’s scope.
Advertisement is not authorization.
Contract and resource validation are still required.
3B.hint: What did the user actually authorize?
3B.solution: Keep the response as evidence, validate its contract, and deny deletion before execution.

6A.title: Detect temporal contamination
6A.context: Customer profiles computed through December are used to predict November purchases. The author randomly splits transaction rows.
options: Choose a feature cutoff before outcome events
Split customers/documents or time according to deployment
Keep future transactions because they improve accuracy
Fit preprocessing on the training partition
feedback: Future outcomes must not appear in features.
The split must reflect the generalization claim.
This is leakage, not useful predictive information.
Preprocessing can also leak holdout information.
6A.hint: Could each feature have existed at prediction time?
6A.solution: Define a historical cutoff, rebuild features from earlier events, reserve later outcomes, and isolate preprocessing.

6B.title: Read the latency budget
6B.context: A trace shows queue=850 ms, prefill=400 ms, first decode=50 ms, remaining decode=1,100 ms.
feedback: This ignores queueing and prefill.
Arrival-to-first-token includes queue, prefill, and first decode; full completion adds the rest.
Queue and first decode were omitted.
6B.hint: Start the clock at request arrival.
6B.solution: TTFT=850+400+50=1,300 ms. Total=1,300+1,100=2,400 ms; a two-second completion SLO is breached.
